findings.description: The instance user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in plain text. User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute (and from the instance metadata service itself), so these long-lived credentials are effectively disclosed and must be treated as compromised.

No metadata_options block is set, so the instance permits IMDSv1 unauthenticated metadata requests. A server-side request forgery in the Apache application would let an attacker retrieve instance role credentials.
The instance does not configure root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root EBS volume (which also holds the user-data-derived configuration) may be stored unencrypted.

The instance is launched in a public subnet with automatic public IP assignment and an internet gateway route, placing it directly on the internet alongside a wide-open security group instead of behind a load balancer in a private subnet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is deliberately commented out), so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted and is not protected by a KMS key.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and specifies no KMS encryption, so a copy of the volume's data persists unencrypted and can be shared or restored without key-based access control.
Ingress on TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access on the internet-facing instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration path and outbound command-and-control channel from a compromised host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with no HTTPS listener configured anywhere, so all traffic to the web host traverses the internet unencrypted and is subject to interception and tampering.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so every instance placed in this subnet receives a public IP address and is reachable from the internet rather than being isolated in a private network layer.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so instances launched in this subnet are automatically given public IPs and exposed to inbound internet traffic.

The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration or KMS key), so network audit logs are stored without enforced encryption.

No public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restriction is defined for the flow log bucket, so account or bucket-level settings alone govern whether the network logs become publicly or cross-account readable.
The audit log bucket sets force_destroy = true and has no versioning, MFA delete, or object lock, allowing flow log evidence to be deleted or overwritten and destroying the audit trail.
